cells.tense: Right here, something long pressed for is running on its own now and steady, and what's yours is still in your hands.
cells.ask: Say the direction out loud once — to one person or to the page — just as it stands. What that gives back is a place it now exists outside your head.
cells.core:
Most days here things move because you've kept the proportions right — adding a little, letting a little go, shifting when what's around you shifts — and that keeping is the work. Nothing about that has stalled. What you're inside of is the stretch of that doing well: it doesn't need your whole weight on it, and it's still moving.

The open thing isn't the moving, it's how little of it gets said. Say the direction out loud once, somewhere it can be heard, and set it down as it stands. What that gives back is that the thing now exists somewhere other than inside your keeping of it.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping it steady, and you know you are.
cells.verb: carry a direction steadily enough that it no longer needs to be argued for
cells.place: the ongoing work of keeping the blend right as things shift

cells.tense: You're already standing somewhere this hasn't arrived at yet, steering by what's not here.
cells.ask: Put in front of you the three things pulling at once, in writing, and cross off the one no one's actually waiting on. What that gives back is one direction instead of three.
cells.core:
On an ordinary good day you sense what's needed and give it, hold back what isn't, and the whole thing keeps flowing — you can change directions mid-step and nothing knocks loose.

What's happening instead is that you're adjusting to things that haven't happened — a wobble you can feel coming, a mood that might turn, a gap you might leave — and the correcting has taken the place of the task. Every adjustment fastens onto the next one, and none of them land, because the thing you're correcting toward isn't here yet. Put the pulls in front of you, in writing, and cross off the one no one's actually waiting on. What that gives back is a direction you can act on while it's still today.
cells.sheetLine: You're steadying things that haven't wobbled yet.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that's already shut, still deciding how to leave the room.
cells.ask: Put one hour on a calendar today for the project that's been waiting, and keep it whatever else comes up. What that gives back is that something you chose gets to move before the week does.
cells.core:
When this part runs well, adjusting is what it's for: you change the mix quickly, undo what you just did without ceremony, and afterward you don't keep score. It looks like nothing, and it's how the days keep their line.

What's happening instead is that the settling only goes backward — to the move you wish you hadn't made, the moment a thing shifted. Changing course now would mean admitting what's gone came loose from your hands, so nothing gets moved into. That's why decisions keep waiting for a better day than this one. Give one hour to something that's been waiting, today, whatever else comes up and whatever else it costs. Not because it's owed — because movement you chose is the first thing you'd recognize as yours again.
cells.sheetLine: You've been holding the last mistake instead of the next move.

cells.tense: The adjusting is still running in the room, and nobody has put your name on it, including you.
cells.ask: Write one line — "I'm the one who keeps this steady" — about something you've been calling just the situation. What that gives back is that the keeping stops being invisible to you, today.
cells.core:
What you do here on a Wednesday is tune: you catch a wobble early and correct it before anyone else notices, give the thing that's short a little more room, tilt back when it's had enough. When that's going well, people around you only feel the even part, and that's the closest it gets to a mark of yours most days.

What doesn't happen is you counting it. You talk about the adjustments as the work or as what the moment asks for, and the one who keeps reading the room goes unlisted. Yet it's already shaping how those days run. Take something you've been calling the situation and write it as yours — the keeping of it, that you do. What that gives back, today, is that what you're making becomes something you can point at.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one keeping it steady, and you haven't claimed it yet.
